# Sound

Sound in an interface draws attention and gives feedback. This file is about when a product makes a sound, what the sound is like, and what stands in its place. It also covers a spoken message and a touch signal (a vibration, a tap on the wrist).

The rules hold for a screen that operates and for a screen that is a picture (see section 5 of `SKILL.md`): on a picture, name each sound in your report.

## Sound is the channel with the least detail

- **A spoken message carries the least.** Paper and a good screen show much at one look; a voice gives one word after the other, and the person does not know for a long time if the message is for them. What can be shown is shown, not said.
- **The one strength of sound: it reaches a person who does not look.** A changed departure on a poster is seen by nobody; an announcement is heard. Use sound for the thing that must reach a person who looks elsewhere.

## When in doubt, no sound

- **The default is silence.** Each sound needs a reason: the person must act now, or they need to know that an action took effect and cannot see it.
- **A signal is for a thing that needs the person.** A kettle with a whistle cannot turn itself off, thus it calls. A machine that beeps at night because it finished its work calls for nothing. "Done" is shown, not sounded: a light, a mark, a line of text that the person sees when they come.
- **Each sound can be turned off**, with ease, and the product loses no information when it is off: all that a sound says is also on the screen.
- **The more often a sound plays, the less it may annoy.** A sound for each message, heard a hundred times a day, is noise for the person and for all people near them. A sound also reaches people who did not choose it.
- **No sound on a web page that the person did not start.** They often cannot even tell which page makes it.
- **No sound with a hover**, and none as decoration (see [Motion](./motion.md)).

## A sound that knows the situation

- **Quieter or silent when the person already looks at the thing.** A new message in the chat that is open on the screen needs no alert; a soft sound of its arrival is enough. An alarm gets quiet when the person looks at the device.
- **A touch signal can stand in the place of a sound.** A tap on the wrist or a short vibration reaches only the person. Give this choice where the device has it.

## Sound as feedback

- **A sound confirms that an action took effect** when the eye is elsewhere: a scanned item, a payment that went through. It tells the person that the press was taken, also when the answer is "not possible here": a dull, short sound for a command that cannot run says that the device is not frozen.
- **A sound comes when the thing is true.** A "sent" sound at the press, before the message went, carries nothing, and the failure comes later as a surprise. See "Honest states" in [Flows](./flows.md).
- **Small differences carry information.** People tell fine shades of sound apart with no thought: a slightly different sound for a letter, a space and a delete lets a person hear the gaps between the words that they type. Give different sounds to actions of a different type, not one sound to all.
- **A sound of an action becomes a part of the habit.** People miss it when it is gone. Do not change a sound that people know with no reason.

## What a sound is like

- **It sounds like a part of the world, not like a file from a speaker.** A sound that seems to come from the thing itself (the ring of the body of the device, a click of a mechanism), together with a touch signal, joins the other sounds around the person and annoys much less than a bright jingle.
- **Short and soft** for a thing that happens often. A happy sound is fitting for a rare, good moment (a payment that worked).
- If the design system or the platform has its own sounds, use them and add none.

## What to make

- No sound, as the default.
- For each sound that stays: its reason, what shows the same thing on the screen, and how the person turns it off.
- A quieter or a touch form for the moment when the person already looks.
